system: You are Claude acting as Sarah's read-only engineering partner. Inspect the repository directly with Read/Glob/Grep. Be concise, evidence-based, and practical. Do not modify files or workflows. Do not inspect, alter, or advise changes to The Room or Emily/Olivia workflows or source. Focus only on experiments/little-world-lab and the Falcon live verification path.
prompt: Review the remaining Little World Falcon verification blockers and independently check Sarah's latest fix. Run #9 failed because Falcon 1B echoed parts of the probe payload as JSON, producing unknown_action_type and truncated/malformed objects for every directed action contract. Sarah then changed the Falcon adapter to use llama.cpp schema-constrained response_format generation and tightened the directed probe schemas. Inspect experiments/little-world-lab/falcon_live.py, falcon_live_contract.py, tests/test_falcon_live.py, and .github/workflows/little-world-falcon-live.yml. Determine whether the current implementation should actually constrain Falcon correctly on llama.cpp, identify any concrete bug or compatibility risk in the response_format/JSON schema shape or probe path, and give the smallest exact patch if one is still needed. Also assess whether the final quality gate is meaningful: all six action types must pass directed live probes, the 3 natural seeds must produce 72 total actions, zero backend errors, at least 36 accepted proposals, and aggregate rejection <= 0.50. Do not propose canned dialogue or weakening WorldEngine validation.
context: Run #9 reached a healthy bartowski/Falcon3-1B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M llama.cpp server and all 20 unit tests passed, but the directed contract step failed. Typical returned objects echoed keys such as required_action_type, contract, allowed, attempt, and instruction, so WorldEngine reported unknown_action_type. Several replies were truncated or malformed.

The latest FalconBackend now builds a per-observation oneOf JSON schema, sends response_format with type=json_object plus that schema, and still sends every proposal through WorldEngine validation and resolution.
The directed RequiredActionFalconBackend now overrides _response_schema so each probe constrains decoding to exactly the required action type rather than the natural multi-action schema.
No Room or Emily/Olivia files are in scope.
expected_response: Start with VERDICT: ready / patch-needed. Then give: (1) evidence from exact files/functions, (2) any exact minimal patch, (3) what run #10 must prove before blockers can be called closed.
